To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients with depression value practitioners with a positive attitude, who listen and collaborate.

patients with depression particularly valued practitioner attributes that were based on the practitioner’s bearing, including the practitioner’s demeanour, and the practitioner’s enabling role, including the practitioner encouraging and enabling patients to take greater responsibility for their own recovery.

patients value practitioners that: ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: 1) are approachable and have an easy manner; 2) share relevant personal information; ::: ::: ::: ::: and 3) are interested and accept the patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how practitioners can establish effective relationships with patients with depression.
the practitioner–patient encounter, and the attributes that patients value in their practitioners.
the practitioner attributes that patients value, and the implications for practitioners and policy makers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
patients with depression value the way in which practitioners communicate with them and the way in which they are enabled to engage in their own recovery.
the attributes of the practitioner that patients value are those that promote the patient's sense of self-worth and self-efficacy.
patients value the practitioner attributes of bearing, manner and enabling role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
practitioners should be aware of the importance they can have on the treatment of depression and that they should strive to establish and maintain good relationships with their patients.
practitioners who show interest, acceptance and empathy and are willing to collaborate and encourage self-care are more likely to engage their patients and help them to achieve the best outcomes.

the practitioner attributes patients with a diagnosis of depression most value are those that demonstrate a practitioner's ability to listen and respond to the needs of their patients, and to provide them with the tools and support they need to engage with their treatment and to manage their condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients value practitioners' bearing, and that this is more important than the specific treatment a practitioner can offer.
practitioners should be mindful of their manner when interacting with patients and that they should be prepared to share relevant personal information and to collaborate on manageable goals.
practitioners should focus on their manner and their role in enabling patients with depression to engage in treatment.
